title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is item 3 of a list in Grothendieck's manuscript on Gauss–Manin connections, stratifications and crystals. On the preceding page he describes a 'universal' way to build integrable stratifications. Take a smooth S-group G, a G_X-torsor P on X and a representation of G on a module F over S. The constant module F_X carries its canonical stratification, which G_X preserves. Twisting by P, i.e. forming P ∧^{G_X} F_X, produces an O_X-module with integrable (relative) stratification. Over a field k, with X geometrically connected and x a rational point, he expects modules with 'integrable stratification' to be equivalent to finite-dimensional representations of a generalized (pro-)group Π_1(X,x). This is a Tannakian description.

On the next page, 'intégrable' for an invertible stratified L means that L^{⊗n} is trivial as a stratified module for some n prime to p. So in this text an integrable stratification is one that becomes trivial on a finite étale cover, i.e. it has finite étale (prime-to-p) monodromy.

This page is the relative version over an arbitrary base S.
- Fix a set 𝕃 of primes and a base point. This can be a section e of X/S or, more generally, a closed subscheme Σ ⊂ X that is finite, radicial and surjective over S. Each geometric fibre of Σ is then a single point, so Σ serves as a base point even when no section exists.
- Assume X → S is flat, of finite presentation, with geometrically connected fibres.
- Assume a relative pro-𝕃 fundamental group π_1^𝕃(X,e) exists as a pro-group over S.
- Conjecture (marked '?'): representations of π_1^𝕃(X,e) on modules over S are equivalent to O_X-modules with integrable stratification relative to S. The latter are required to correspond, on each geometric fibre, to a representation of π_1(X_s̄) that factors through an 𝕃-group.

General form of the conjecture:
- Let Π be a strict pro-(étale group) over S and P a pro-torsor under Π_X on X.
- Require that on each geometric fibre, Π_s̄ appears as a quotient of the fundamental group of X_s̄.
- Then the functor V ↦ P ∧^{Π_X} V_X should give an equivalence between (1) continuous representations of Π in modules over S and (2) stratified O_X-modules (relative to S) whose fibrewise monodromy is 'subordinate to' the quotient Π_s̄ of π_1(X_s̄).

In modern terms this is a relative Tannakian / étale Riemann–Hilbert statement for stratified (D-) modules with finite étale monodromy in families. Its absolute case over a field is the Gieseker-type correspondence: stratified bundles trivialised on a finite étale cover ↔ representations of π_1^ét with finite image. The relative case is close to later work of dos Santos, Esnault–Hai and others on relative stratified fundamental group schemes.
errors: Stated only as an expectation with a '?' in the margin; no proof is sketched.

Existence of a relative pro-𝕃 fundamental group π_1^𝕃(X,e) over S is merely assumed. Without properness or tameness hypotheses, prime-to-p fundamental groups are not locally constant in families (cf. SGA1 X, XIII), so the hypothesis carries real content.

Full faithfulness of V ↦ P∧V_X needs Π_s̄ → quotient of π_1(X_s̄) to behave well (surjectivity, connected fibres). Essential surjectivity needs stratified modules to be trivialised on a pro-étale cover that descends to the torsor P. For non-coherent 'modules ab.' or non-flat representations, base change of horizontal sections may also cause trouble. None of this is addressed.
Over an imperfect base or in mixed characteristic, the relationship between 'stratification relative to S' and 'trivial on a finite étale cover' is not spelled out on this page.

ideas.what: Integrable stratified modules (trivialised on finite étale covers) ↔ representations of the étale fundamental group (finite/profinite monodromy) — absolute case
ideas.modern_name: Stratified bundles with finite monodromy; Gieseker's correspondence; Tannakian fundamental group of stratified sheaves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gieseker (1975); dos Santos (2007); Esnault–Mehta (2010) for the converse direction (Gieseker conjecture)
ideas.where_published: Crystals discussed in Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (1968); this specific statement unsure

ideas.what: Relative version over arbitrary base S: representations of a relative pro-𝕃 fundamental group (or a strict pro-étale group Π with torsor P) in modules over S ↔ relatively stratified O_X-modules with fibrewise 𝕃-monodromy, via twisting by the torsor
ideas.modern_name: Relative Tannakian duality for stratified sheaves / relative fundamental group schemes; étale Riemann–Hilbert in families
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (relative Tannakian categories, 1990); dos Santos; Esnault–Hai (fundamental groupoid scheme, ~2008); later work on relative stratified fundamental groups

ideas.what: Using a finite radicial surjective subscheme Σ ⊂ X over S as a substitute base point when no section exists
ideas.modern_name: Base 'point' given by a radicial multisection / fibre functor at a radicial point; universal homeomorphism invariance of π_1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in SGA1 (topological invariance of étale site under radicial surjective maps)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 IX / SGA4 VIII for topological invariance; this use as base point unsure

ideas.what: Construction of stratified modules by twisting constant modules by group-scheme torsors (P ∧^{Π_X} V_X)
ideas.modern_name: Associated bundle / Tannakian fibre functor from torsor
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Nori's fundamental group scheme 1976/82 uses the same mechanism)

missed.claim: A conjectural relative equivalence (circa 1972), with explicit hypotheses: flat finitely presented X/S, geometrically connected fibres, base point given by a section or a finite radicial surjective Σ, and a chosen set of primes 𝕃. It relates relatively stratified modules with fibrewise 𝕃-finite monodromy to representations of a relative pro-𝕃 fundamental group, or of any strict pro-étale group Π with a pro-torsor that is fibrewise a quotient of π_1. This anticipates by decades the relative Tannakian theory of stratified bundles.
missed.quote: la cat. des représentations linéaires de π_1^𝕃(X,e) dans les modules ... sur S doit être équivalente à celle des Modules ... sur X à stratification intégrable rel/S, qui sur chaque fibre géométrique correspondent à une représentation du groupe fondamental qui se factorise via un 𝕃-groupe
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Relative stratified fundamental groups and families versions of Gieseker-type correspondences are active topics (dos Santos, Esnault–Hai, Kindler, etc.). The formulation with an arbitrary torsor P and the subordination condition per fibre is a clean general statement. It may not be literally stated in that form in the literature and shows Grothendieck's early priority.

deep.surprise_reason: An early (c.1972) and fairly precise conjecture of a relative étale Riemann–Hilbert / Tannakian correspondence for stratified modules with finite 𝕃-monodromy, including the radicial-multisection base point. It anticipates Gieseker (1975) and later relative work, but it is a sketch with a '?', and the absolute case is now standard.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'donnant un faisceau[?] 𝕃 de nombres premiers' is more likely '[se] donnant un ensemble 𝕃 de nombres premiers', continuing 'en' from the previous page.
Lines 2–3: 'obtiendrons[?] ! une section e' probably reads 'obtenu à l'aide d'une section e de X/S' (unsure).
Insertion over 'π_1^𝕃(X,e)' reads 'profini' (pro-groupe profini) rather than a generic 'pro-groupe'.
'S localement (?)' is probably 'S localement noethérien' or similar; the '(?)' is a marginal query mark.
'modules abéliens sur S' / 'Modules ab.' may instead be 'modules cohérents' / 'Modules coh.' — the handwriting is ambiguous.
'groupe fondamental pro-alg.[?]' is uncertain; possibly 'groupe fondamental géométrique' or 'profini'.
